newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Yugoslavia warcrimes trial hears last witness.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslavia warcrimes trial hears last witness.

text.p: The United Nations tribunal for former Yugoslavia on Thursday wound up witness testimony in the trial of a Bosnian Serb accused of committing atrocities against Moslems and Croats early in the Bosnian conflict.
Gabrielle Kirk McDonald, presiding judge in the five-month-old trial of Dusan Tadic, said she was calling a 17-day adjournment before closing arguments on November 25.
"It's been a long trial with the number of exhibits and thousands of pages of testimony," McDonald said.

Alfred Huebel, a German police chief who interviewed Tadic after his arrest in Munich in 1994, was the last witness to take the stand in the trial, the first war crimes case since the Nuremberg and Tokyo trials after World War Two.
Since May 7 the court has heard 125 witnesses, amassed more than 6,000 pages of transcripts and received more than 500 exhibits in evidence.
In a surprise move on Thursday morning, lawyers for the defence said they would not be recalling any witnesses.
Earlier the court heard witness for the prosecution Sofia Tadic, the ex-wife of Tadic's brother Mladen.

Tadic's former sister-in-law alleged he was a fervent nationalist who had no Muslim friends, but during cross-examination by defence barrister Steven Kay conceded a Muslim had helped carry the coffin at Tadic's father's funeral.
McDonald said closing arguments later this month had been scheduled to take two days.
